details: CONFIRMED by measurement. Where the guard file's git starts go: TestMergeJudges.merge_accepts runs, for each of the 10
CASES, a full flow (item commit on main, a new worktree, rq.take, a test commit, a review, a check record with a gate log
and a mark, a close commit, the merge hook), and TestDoneJudges runs rq.done 10 times. None of that is built from a
template, so building `main` by copy changes about 1% of the file's git starts. The brief named this file first and its
failing case is this file; the pass case asked for the starts and wall time measured before and after. The fix item
would be closed with its failing case still failing.
evidence: base worktree: git worktree add --detach <scratch>/base $(git merge-base master HEAD)
git diff --stat master...HEAD: tests/test_guard_test_name.py is not in the change.
failing_case: Merge base vs HEAD 6cb1fbd3, run side by side under the same load with a git-counting shim on PATH:
pytest -q tests/test_guard_test_name.py
base: 1191 git starts, 3 passed in 30.07 s
HEAD: 1178 git starts, 3 passed in 30.53 s
The queue item's failing case (one test starts 1524 git in 91 s) is the file the change was taken to fix; it is untouched
by the change, and the template saves only the 3-4 git calls of building `main` per Flow case. The builder's report says
"guard test file 91s -> 11s": with both trees under the same load the time is equal, so that figure compared runs at
different machine loads. Expected: the guard file's git starts fall by a large share (the brief's measure), and the before
and after numbers are recorded.
fix_hint: In TestMergeJudges build the checked branch once (one item, one take, the test commit, one check record) and for each
name only reset the worktree to that checked state and write the close commit, as TestDoneJudges already does with
`git reset --hard HEAD~1`; or seed the 10 items in one template seed. Then measure the three named files before and after.
pass_cases: 1. pytest tests/test_guard_test_name.py with a git-counting shim: HEAD starts at most half the git processes of the merge
base (1191 measured there), all 3 tests pass.
2. TestMergeJudges still asserts, for each of the 10 CASES, that the merge hook's step_queue accepts exactly the names
holds_test accepts (refusal text "closed without a test" for the rest).
3. TestDoneJudges still asserts rq.done accepts and refuses the same CASES.
4. The before/after git starts and wall time of the three files the brief names (guard, queue, gate) are written in the
fixer's report, measured side by side at the same load.
reason: tests/test_guard_test_name.py TestMergeJudges builds the branch once: 484 git starts vs 1191 at base (under half), 3 passed; the other cases keep their assertions; before/after numbers in the fix report.
findings.summary: the brief's failing case is not fixed: test_guard_test_name.py still starts about 1180 git processes (1191 before, 1178 after) and takes the same time; the reported 91 s -> 11 s does not reproduce
